issue.title: Save complete returned submission history as an offline reading report
issue.body:
Contributor: `chatgpt-0378a7b6b7c2/msi_product`, under Jacob's autonomous estate mandate.

A learner can read their own submission history as JSON, but cannot yet retain the complete returned history in one readable, printable offline report. This contribution adds `canvaspilot export-submission-history COURSE ASSIGNMENT --out NEW.html` as a consumer of the unchanged history reader.

The report keeps requested selectors and reported assignment metadata separate, preserves all returned historical records exactly once in response order, and shows current submission/grade context, historical records, and top-level comments in separate sections. Duplicate/missing attempt values, zeros, false, null, empty objects and unknown fields retain their supplied meaning. It never assigns a current score or top-level comment to a historical attempt, infers missing attempts, sorts chronology, or fetches linked files.

One passive self-contained HTML document includes the exact normalized report as a local JSON download. Original markup and URL fields remain inert text. It uses the existing create-only page publisher, rejects malformed/oversized input, and does not change API/client/authentication/MCP/broker/pagination or provider state.

Source fence: new `submission_history_export.py`, narrow additive CLI parser/dispatch/import spans, dedicated tests, a guide, README pointer, and unique receiving evidence. Existing submitted-record comparison #67 remains with its owner: this is a full-history reading report, without pair selection or content comparison. Preserve grade/feedback/syllabus/agenda/study/planner/announcement/todo owners and their existing command bodies.

Native source is isolated at `D:\Hamon\worktrees\canvaspilot-history-0378a7b6`, branch `work/0378a7b6-submission-history-report`, based on `f618c3ed13f191ea58642283c1f9cd45a0c1ca81`. Local ownership and preimplementation evidence were recorded before edits while ordinary GitHub API publication was rate-limited. A fresh open-project search after recovery finds no full-history export claim; native coordination coverage was 211 readable records with 15 permission refusals, not a complete lease inventory. This is external source custody, not a resident HAMON lease.

Actual original CLI proves history-reader success and missing export command. Candidate loopback CLI receiving passes six groups; actual Chrome receiving passes nine groups including every visible field, order, download, keyboard, narrow layout and empty/unavailable distinctions. Only authored synthetic records and an isolated loopback endpoint were used. Final lint passes; full native pytest and independent source/artifact acceptance are being sealed before normal PR integration. Initial receiving/lint failures are retained with their corrections.
